TheMughal Empire
Later Mughals
BahadurShah-l(1707-1712AD)
BahadurShah-I followeda policy of compromise and
tried to reconcile with Rajputs, Marathas,Jats and the
Sikhs who became very powerful.However, Bahadur
Shah's policy of compromise ended in a failure which
precipitated the decline of the Mughal Empire. After
ruling for less than five years, Bahadur Shah-l was
succeeded by his son Jahandar Shah in 1712, whose reign
was even less fortunate than his father's. Nevertheless,
Bahadur Shai-!
Mughalrulecontinued toexist.
As a matterof fact,theunsettled political and militaryconditionsof theMughal Empire
also attracted some foreign invaders such as Nadir Shah who was the ruler of Persia.
Unfortunately, the successors of Bahadur Shah-I became mere pawns in the tussle of
power of 18th-century India and ultimately failed to stop the invasions and internal
rebellions.
Ruleof JahandarShah couldnot continue long and in theyear1713AD he wasdefeated
byhis nephewFarrukh Siyar whobecame thenext rulerwith thehelp of Syed Brothers.
He ruled for the next six years when in 1719 Muhammad Shah came to throne.
Period of Muhammad Shah (from 1719 to 1748)was theperiod of the rise of many
independent states like Bengal and Oudh.Muhammad Shah was succeeded by following
rulers who weremostly inefficient as comparedto the earlier Mughals:
AhmadShah (1748-1754)
Alamgirll(1754-1759)
ShahAlamll(1759-1806)
BahadurShahZafar(1837-1857)
